summary: Iteration 2 verification pass on the /dashboard skeleton-flash fix, focused on what changed since my iteration-1 handoff (verifier-2026-09-20T135629Z.json): the HIGH back/forward-staleness fix, the DashboardData extraction to src/db/dashboard.ts::buildDashboardPayload, and the BetaBanner prop change. All three hold up under independent re-verification; nothing re-litigated from iteration 1 beyond a light-touch rendering-mode re-check as instructed. (1) STALENESS FIX: read DashboardBody.tsx's actual current code (not the handoff prose) line by line. Confirmed FetchState only ever transitions to 'loading' once, in the initial useState seed, and only when initialData === null; fetchDashboard() (the function the background-revalidation effect calls) has no code path that sets status:'loading' — it only ever calls setFetchState with {status:'success', data} or via errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded(message), which returns prev unchanged when prev.status==='success'. The revalidation effect (`useEffect(() => { if (authLoading) return; if (!user||!token) return; fetchDashboard(); }, [authLoading, user, token, fetchDashboard])`) is unconditional on initialData — confirmed no `if (initialData !== null) return` guard exists anywhere in the file. Independently mutation-tested the new test file myself (not just re-run): (a) reintroduced the iteration-1 `if (initialData !== null) return;` guard at the top of the revalidation effect, re-ran tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx -- went red (`expected vi.fn() to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` on the 'fetches /api/dashboard even though initialData was server-resolved' test), confirming the test would have caught the iteration-1 regression; (b) restored that guard removal, then reverted errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded to unconditionally return {status:'error', message} regardless of prev -- re-ran the same file, went red on a different test ('keeps the painted content when a background revalidation fails', got 'Network error' text and no '3–1' content), confirming that helper is load-bearing too; (c) restored both changes byte-identical to the version I first read (diffed by grep against my initial Read output -- identical) and re-ran the full test file plus dashboardBody.test.tsx -- 6/6 green. Given both load-bearing pieces of the claimed fix are independently proven necessary by mutation-testing the REAL component (not a reimplementation), and this corroborates two prior independent live-browser probes (software-engineer's iteration-2 controlled A/B probe, qa-acceptance's iteration-1 Next.js-source-backed repro) that are consistent with this code, I did not re-run a third live-browser probe of my own -- judged the marginal evidence value low relative to cost given the DOM-mutation-test already isolates and confirms the exact two claimed mechanisms. (2) buildDashboardPayload: diffed app/app/dashboard/page.tsx against HEAD (`git diff`) -- the extraction replaces the pre-refactor inline Promise.all block with a single buildDashboardPayload(uid, email) call; read src/db/dashboard.ts directly and confirmed it performs the identical 5 reads (prisma.user.findUnique, getUserFreeClimbRecord, getUserClimbReplays, getDuelStats, getRecentDuelsForUser), identical .catch() fallbacks, and identical duelStats narrowing to {wins, losses, current_streak, best_streak} that I already field-verified against DuelRecordCard/DuelRecordData and prisma/schema.prisma's DuelStats model in iteration 1 -- re-confirmed schema.prisma:DuelStats still has exactly wins/losses/current_streak/best_streak plus the dropped user_id and updated_at, so the narrowing is unchanged and complete. For route.ts's shape change (duelStats now narrowed instead of the raw Prisma row): grepped the whole repo for 'duelStats' and for '/api/dashboard' -- the only two consumers are app/app/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx (typed against the same DashboardData interface, reads only the 4 narrowed fields) and app/mobile/src/contexts/AppDataContext.tsx, whose own locally-declared `DashboardData` interface (line 29-38) has no duelStats field at all (only user + freeClimb) -- read that interface directly, confirmed it cannot read user_id/updated_at because it never references duelStats. No other file references GET /api/dashboard's response. Confirmed safe. (3) BetaBanner: grepped for all usages -- only app/app/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx (the one caller, passing token) and the component's own definition; no other caller to break. Read BetaBanner.tsx's handleSubmit -- `if (!token) return;` guards the only token-dependent code path, and the Join button is `disabled={state==='loading' || token===null}`, so clicking with token null is a no-op guarded twice (disabled attribute + early return). No runtime issue. (4) Rendering mode: light-touch re-check per task instruction -- one clean `rm -rf .next && pnpm build` in the main app tree, confirmed `ƒ /dashboard` in the route table (not `○`), and confirmed via a small node script against .next/prerender-manifest.json that '/dashboard' is absent from both routes and dynamicRoutes. Reverted the resulting app/next-env.d.ts churn from my own build afterward; no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md were generated since I only ran `pnpm build`, not `pnpm start`/`pnpm dev`. (5) Full gate suite re-run by me from the current working tree: app-lint clean (0 warnings), app-typecheck clean, app-test 82 files / 751 tests all green (includes both new dashboardBody.test.tsx and dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx), orchestrator-typecheck clean, orchestrator-test 58/58 green, pack-hygiene 0 violations (8 agent files). Did not commit or push. Working tree left exactly as found (git status --short after my run shows only the same pre-existing uncommitted changes from software-engineer's iteration-2 pass, no next-env.d.ts or other churn from my own commands).

learnings.insight: app/tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx is a genuine mutation-proof gate for both load-bearing pieces of the staleness fix, not just a happy-path assertion: independently confirmed (not just re-run) that reintroducing the iteration-1 `initialData !== null` guard on the revalidation effect fails test 1, and that reverting `errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded`'s functional-updater (prev.status==='success' -> keep prev) to an unconditional error-set fails test 2. Both mutations were applied directly to the real DashboardBody.tsx, tested, and reverted -- this is stronger evidence than re-running software-engineer's own claimed mutation results.
learnings.action: Treat this test file as a real regression gate for any future touch to DashboardBody's fetch/effect logic -- a change that silently reintroduces either defect will fail it.

learnings.insight: Confirmed end-to-end that the API-route response-shape change (duelStats now narrowed to 4 fields instead of the raw Prisma row) is safe: the only two consumers of GET /api/dashboard are the web DashboardBody (typed against the same shared DashboardData interface the route now returns) and mobile's AppDataContext, whose own independently-declared DashboardData interface never references duelStats at all. No `as` cast anywhere reads the dropped user_id/updated_at fields.
